title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 47
paragraphs: Both sides, then, were content to do this, and as dawn appeared they began exchanging their positions with one another. But the Boeotians, perceiving what was being done, reported it to Mardonius, who on hearing it at once tried to change positions himself, bringing the Persians across so as to face the Lacedaemonians. When Pausanias learned that this was being done, he perceived that he was not unobserved, and led the Spartans back again to the right wing; and Mardonius likewise returned to his left.
